reason: The text does not describe the regular people as antagonistic to their leaders. When Gedaliah is appointed as governor, the military commanders and people come to him peacefully and he swears an oath to them. After Gedaliah's assassination by Ishmael son of Nethaniah, the people's subsequent flight to Egypt is explicitly motivated by fear of the Chaldeans ('כִּי יָרְא֖וּ מִפְּנֵי כַשְׂדִּֽים' - 'because they feared the presence of the Chaldeans'), not antagonism toward their leadership. The passage focuses on external military threats and political succession rather than popular opposition to leaders.
